key_insight: Gradient-aware AI agents can autonomously propose, train, and revise turbulence closures using feedback from a differentiable CFD solver.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce manual effort in developing turbulence models while improving agreement with reference flow statistics.
method: Use a multi-agent LLM system to search analytical, neural, and hybrid closure forms.
Embed proposals in GPU-native differentiable CFD, define objectives, and validate gradient paths.
Use truncated-horizon gradients for a posteriori training and guide subsequent proposals with simulation feedback.
evidence_signal: Tests cover 2D turbulence dissipation and subgrid-scale closures plus 3D channel-flow wall models; gradient-based training recovers reference coefficients not reached by forward evaluation alone within the same budget.
watch_item: Truncated-horizon gradients enable training under chaotic dynamics, but performance beyond the tested flows and targeted statistics remains unestablished.
paper_title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
